subject: Cannot estimate Multivariate Normal covariance matrix correctly

messages.author: 7244b7b0d6d98e71
messages.subject: Cannot estimate Multivariate Normal covariance matrix correctly
parts:
Dear all, 

I am trying to fit a really simple two-outcome hierarchical model with two random intercepts correlated with each other. Later to intended to more outcomes and more random terms. Right now I am simulating the data with really simple setups.

However, so far I got trouble to get the correct covariance matrix and correlation even for two random effects. The fixed effects are alway estimated correctly.

$Y_1 = X \beta + U_1 | id$
$Y_2 = X \beta + U_2 | id$

$U = (U1,  U2) \sim MVN(\pmb 0, \Sigma)$

```
JMcode <- nimbleCode({
   
    sigma1 ~ dinvgamma(0.0001, 0.0001)
    sigma2 ~ dinvgamma(0.0001, 0.0001)

    R[1:2, 1:2] <- diag(2)
    D[1:2, 1:2] ~ dwish(R = R[1:2, 1:2], df = 4)
   
    betas1[1:p] ~ dmnorm(zeros1[1:p], omega1[1:p, 1:p])
    betas2[1:q] ~ dmnorm(zeros2[1:q], omega2[1:q, 1:q])
       
    for (j1 in 1:n1) {
        mu1[j1] <- inprod(betas1[1:p], X1[j1, 1:p]) + u[id[j1], 1]
        y[j1, 1] ~ dnorm(mu1[j1], sd = sigma1)
       
        mu2[j1] <- inprod(betas2[1:q], X2[j1, 1:q]) + u[id[j1], 2]
        y[j1, 2] ~ dnorm(mu2[j1], sd = sigma2)
    }
   
    for (i in 1:N) {
        u[i, 1:2] ~ dmnorm(zerou[1:2], D[1:2, 1:2])
    }

    Cov[1:2, 1:2] <- inverse(D[1:2, 1:2])
   
  # Scale var/covar matrix to become the correlation matrix
    rho <- Cov[1, 2] / (sqrt(Cov[1, 1]) * sqrt(Cov[2, 2]))
})
```
I got similar problem with INLA and Stan. I am not sure whether it is the problem for my setup. Comparatively, this should be a really simple model.

Thanks a lot for your help.

Sincerely,
Randy

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Cannot estimate Multivariate Normal covariance matrix correctly
parts:
Hi Randy,

Nothing occurs to me in terms of your model structure as to what the problem might be. Are you able to estimate `u` , `sigma1`, `sigma2` and the diagonal elements of `D` reasonably?

Also, in the code you provided, one can't create `X1` and `X2` because the number of rows is not consistent across the items you are cbind'ing together.
So I didn't run your code to see if that indicated anything.

-chris

messages.subject: Re: Cannot estimate Multivariate Normal covariance matrix correctly
parts:
Hi Chris and Thomas,

Thanks a lot for you guys help.
It is a problem with my own simulation on the random effects that I added a constant as random effects.

Now everything works perfectly fine with nimble;-)
The problem is solved. 

Sincerely,
Randy
